children: A USD 4.4 billion stake acquisition in Shriram Finance by MUFG Bank contributed to the investment surge, with Singapore and Mauritius ranking second and third

Japan emerged as India’s largest source of foreign direct investment (FDI) in the first quarter of FY27, with inflows of USD 5.71 billion between April and June 2026. The investment accounted for nearly 29 per cent of India’s total equity FDI inflows of USD 19.81 billion during the quarter, reflecting a significant rise in Japanese capital entering the country.

The quarterly inflow from Japan also exceeded the USD 3.74 billion India received from the country during the whole of FY26. The surge was supported by a major transaction in the financial services sector, as Japanese lender MUFG Bank acquired a 20 per cent stake in Shriram Finance for around USD 4.4 billion.
Singapore was the second-largest source of equity FDI during the quarter, contributing USD 5.22 billion, followed by Mauritius at USD 2.4 billion.
The MUFG Bank transaction accounted for a substantial portion of Japan’s investment during the period and highlighted the role of large financial-sector deals in shaping quarterly FDI rankings.

Japan’s investment relationship with India extends beyond financial services. Manufacturing, semiconductors, batteries, renewable energy and next-generation mobility are among the sectors identified for further cooperation, as both countries seek to strengthen economic ties and diversify supply chains.

The latest figures place Japan ahead of other major investment sources during the quarter, although large individual transactions can significantly influence country-wise FDI totals over shorter periods.

The investment inflows come as India continues to attract overseas capital across financial services, manufacturing and emerging technology sectors. Japan’s position as the leading source in Q1 FY27 reflects the scale of the quarter’s transactions and the potential for further investment across areas of bilateral economic cooperation.
